The policy generates responses and receives gradients. A frozen reference policy defines a behavioral baseline, often the SFT model. A reward model scores responses according to learned preferences. A value model estimates expected returns so advantages can reduce policy-gradient variance. Classic implementations may hold four large networks, but sharing, offloading, or sequential execution can change memory requirements. PPO reuses rollouts with clipped policy ratios and trains the critic on returns. Account separately for policy/critic optimizer state, frozen-model weights, rollout KV caches, and activations. Reward-model quality is a bottleneck: optimizing an imperfect scorer harder can degrade true human-valued behavior.
